heading: Retracting a supporting token withdraws nothing else
text:
### Retracting a supporting token withdraws nothing else [LNOG.4.2]

In a `logical: false` program, retracting the token that supported a rule
firing removes that token and has **no further effect on working
memory**. There is no cascade: nothing is withdrawn, no fact is
retracted as a consequence, and therefore no second retraction can be
triggered by the first.

This follows from there being no logical facts to justify: [LNOG.3.1]
and [LNOG.3.2] make declaring a logical-lifecycle schema and emitting
into one compile errors, so nothing exists for a withdrawal to reach.
It is what makes the retraction path's cost independent of what a rule
has previously emitted — the property [LNOG.5.1]'s `T_retract` bound
rests on.

The reference engine's mechanism is [IRET.8.4].
